newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Research ministers due to agree 4th RTD top-up funds.
newsitem.headline: Research ministers due to agree 4th RTD top-up funds.

text.p: The Research Council is due to reach a common position on Thursday on a draft decision for a financial supplement to the fourth RTD framework programme, EU diplomats said.
The Council asked the European Commission last October to identify money (within category three of 1996 budget ceiling) so that they could decide which areas should get extra money.

A European Commission official said that of the 100 million Ecus under discussion, 35 million had been earmarked for research into Transimissible Spongiform Encephalopathies (TSEs), with nothing extra for vaccines and viral diseases, 20 million for aeronautics research, 12 million for educational multimedia, 12 million for inter-modal transport, 12 million for projects related to water and the environment and nine million for research related to land mines.

Research into TSEs, the family of brain-wasting conditions which includes "mad cow" disease and its human equivalent Creutzfeldt Jacob Disease, would get a further 15 million Ecus from existing Fourth Framework Programme funding, the official said. To this effect, ministers are expected to adopt their draft conclusions on TSEs.
Ministers will also discuss Research Commissioner Edith Cresson's various warm-up papers on how she sees the Fifth Framework Programme developing.
EU President Ireland has asked ministers to consider to what extent research activities in the next programme should be based on Cresson's suggested concentration on six priority topics.
A second question for ministers is what criteria should be used to select research objectives and activities.

Ministers are also due to adopt conclusions on using research to help fight against illegal drug use, a follow up to last year's Madrid summit, a text which will make reference to the possbility of carrying out such work within the planned Fifth RTD Framework Programme.
Another set of conclusions awaiting ministers' scrutiny speaks of encouraging the participation of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in EU research activities.
Ministers are also expected to adopt conclusions on the role of the Joint Research Centre, a text which follows on from the Commission's communication on this topic earlier this year, COM(96)436.

Finally, ministers are due to adopt a decision on the science and technology agreement with South Africa, as detailed in proposal COM(96)423, with a formal ceremony scheduled for 1245 (1145 GMT) on Thursday.

The draft provides for participation in research, shared use of research facilities, exchanges and visits by researchers and other personnel, data exchange and other activities mutually agreed by the parties.
